**Title: The Feathered Insider**

Gary stared at the parrot, a vibrant macaw named Barnaby, who was currently perched on the conference table. Barnaby wasn’t squawking. He was whispering.

"Q3 projections are down by twelve percent," Barnaby said, in Gary’s exact baritone voice. "And tell the CEO his toupee is slipping."

Gary’s blood ran cold. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day. He had promised HR that Barnaby was "low maintenance." He hadn’t promised that Barnaby was a corporate spy with a memory like a steel trap.

"Shh!" Gary hissed, diving under the table. He grabbed Barnaby’s cage, but the bird was too fast. Barnaby hopped onto the shoulder of the CEO, Mrs. Higgins, who was currently reviewing the merger documents.

"Gary is embezzling funds," Barnaby chirped cheerfully. "He buys the good coffee with company money. The dark roast. Not the sludge you drink."

Mrs. Higgins looked up, her eyes narrowing. "Gary? Is this true?"

Gary scrambled out from under the table, hands raised. "No! It’s a glitch! He’s... he’s been listening to my therapy sessions! I talk about money in my sleep!"

Barnaby tilted his head. "Gary’s therapist says he’s afraid of clowns. And that he still sleeps with a nightlight shaped like a duck."

The room went silent. The intern dropped his pen. Mrs. Higgins slowly lowered her glasses.

"Gary," she said, her voice dangerously calm. "Why is the bird wearing my name tag?"

Gary looked down. Barnaby was indeed wearing a tiny, custom-made name tag that read: *Barnaby - Head of Espionage.*

"I... I bought it online as a joke!" Gary stammered.

Barnaby puffed out his chest. "The joke is on you, Gary. Also, the merger is fake. I saw the draft in the trash. It was written in Comic Sans. It’s an insult to the industry."

Mrs. Higgins stood up. "Security! And someone get this bird a lawyer. And a coffee. The good kind."
